findings.title: Plugin request completion logs drop traceID
findings.body: Plugin Request Completed (eventName grafana-data-egress) used to append traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), which includes the ID even when the span is not sampled. That call and the tracing import were removed when the line switched to m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info. instrumentContext only stores endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it does not store traceID, and grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext does not add one either. Info does not take a context.Context, so the span cannot be read at log time unless it was already copied onto the logger. Nothing in this change attaches traceID, so these egress logs can no longer be joined to distributed traces, including unsampled ones.

findings.title: FromContext fallback silently drops request context
findings.body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts infra log's FromContext result to *log.ConcreteLogger. On failure it returns d.New() and ignores ctx. New with no arguments does not read contextual attributes, so pluginId, endpoint, datasource name/UID, and user are omitted while the caller still logs. LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on FromContext for those fields, so this branch emits Plugin Request Completed with no plugin identity and no error. It also throws away the logger infra log returned, even if that value already had the right fields. Fall back to the original wrapper (return d) or otherwise keep ctx, and do not hide the type mismatch.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards receiver and context
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores both the receiver and the context and returns NewTestLogger(), a blank logger. LoggerMiddleware now emits its only line via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so those calls are recorded on the discarded instance. InfoLogs, WarnLogs, and ErrorLogs on the injected TestLogger stay empty, and contextual fields are never applied. That breaks the Logger contract, which says FromContext keeps this logger's context and adds attributes from the given context. Tests using this fake cannot observe plugin request completion logs and will fail if they assert that a line was written.

findings.title: Contextual logging move is untested
findings.body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware is new and has no tests, and the logger middleware change that stopped passing pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, and traceID as explicit log fields is also untested. metrics_middleware_test.go only renames the constructor and still only checks Prometheus series. Nothing asserts that QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics attach those attributes (or that stream RPCs do not), or that Plugin Request Completed still contains them and traceID after FromContext. A wrong attribute list, middleware order, or FromContext implementation would still pass CI.
